free_tier.stated: Storage VPS plans of 0.25 TB (256 GB), 0.5 TB, 1 TB, 2 TB, 3 TB, 4 TB, 6 TB and 8 TB (8192 GB), each a separate VPS; the largest plan is 8 TB. Lithuania, Vilnius. SATA HDD.

egress.terms: Bandwidth allowance per plan: 2 TB, 4 TB, 8 TB, 16 TB, 24 TB, 32 TB, 48 TB and 64 TB on the 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 TB plans; the port is 100 Mbps on each plan. No overage price is published; see limits_note for what happens past the allowance.
egress.free_allowance: 16 TB on the 2 TB plan; 64 TB on the 8 TB plan; 8 TB on the 1 TB plan (monthly allocation)

limits_note: Per-object cap: none stated. Port speed 100 Mbps per VPS. Past the monthly bandwidth allocation the port speed is divided by 10 until next month; no overage price is stated.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form requires an email address, password, first and last name, country, address and city; phone and postal code are optional. The payment methods were not read: unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Established Lithuanian host since 2013. The decisive fact is the pricing structure, not reliability.

dead_end.why: 0.25 TB (256 GB) / 0.5 TB / 1 TB / 8 TB. Lithuania, Vilnius. SATA HDD.

extras.price_verbatim: $4.68/TB/mo on the promo (€4.17), $9.38/TB/mo at renewal (€8.35). At 5 TB: five 1 TB plans at renewal = €41.75 = $46.90/mo = $9.38/TB. At 20 TB: €167 = $187.58/mo = $9.38/TB. This is the cleanest example of the trial-vs-steady-state trap: the advertised €4.17 is a first-term rate against a published 11.99 € list, and the renewal is exactly 2.0x.
